methodological_rigor.justification: Multi-institutional prospective cohort (CKCis) from 15 Canadian centres with 790 localized chRCC patients and median follow-up 4.9 years. A priori selection of pathologic predictors based on prior literature, pre-specified exclusions (pN+ and bilateral tumours from RFS model), sensitivity analyses removing pT stage and pathological size (which were both significant), and appropriate Cox proportional hazards regression. Limitations explicitly acknowledged: no central pathology review, inability to assess proportional hazards assumption due to low event count, wide confidence intervals, no competing risks analysis because of missing cause-of-death data. Reasonable rigor for a real-world retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study provides the largest Canadian chRCC cohort to date with robust 5/10-year outcomes (RFS 93.6%/90.2%; OS 94.5%/83.7%) and identifies clinically actionable predictors (pT stage, sarcomatoid features, margins, necrosis). Directly relevant for argument to avoid lumping chRCC with other non-clear-cell RCC and for designing histology-specific surveillance and future trials. Classified Oxford LoE 2b as a large prospective multi-center cohort with prespecified analysis; the authors note prior benchmark outcomes are similar.

reporting_quality.justification: As a multicentre observational cohort, STROBE applies. Most core items (setting, participants, variables, statistical methods, flow of patients, descriptive results with HRs and 95% CIs) are present, with a patient flow diagram (Figure 1) and clear a priori variable selection. Minor gaps include no explicit STROBE checklist invocation, missing sensitivity analyses table, and limited handling of missing data (e.g., 38 patients with missing cT stage). Data availability via CKCis is institutional/consortium-restricted (data availability score 2); no code shared.

novelty_literature.justification: The analysis is a meaningful extension of prior chRCC cohort studies (MSKCC series by Casuscelli et al., UK-pan-European work by Neves et al.) to a large Canadian multi-centre dataset. Overall survival and recurrence rates are consistent with earlier reports and do not represent a novel biological or therapeutic finding. The identification of sarcomatoid features, necrosis, and positive margins as predictors in chRCC specifically adds incremental granularity and supports calls for histology-specific surveillance guidelines. Not first-in-class but a useful extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well organized, with a coherent narrative linking the lack of chRCC-specific prediction models to the study rationale. Tables and figures (patient flow, KM curves stratified by pT) are referenced in appropriate places. Limitations are transparent. Minor issues: lay-summary abstract repeats some content; one sentence is truncated ('Casuscelli et al. have [REDACTED] and 2016'); isolated minor typos. Overall the paper is very readable.

key_strengths: Large multi-institutional Canadian cohort (n=790) of localized chRCC with 4.9-year median follow-up
A priori selection of predictors with sensitivity analyses for colinearity between pT stage and pathological size
Quantifies effect sizes for sarcomatoid features (HR 7.08), positive margins (HR 4.21), necrosis (HR 3.69), and pT3/T4 (HR 12.20)
Strong argument for chRCC-specific surveillance rather than lumping with non-clear cell RCC
Transparent acknowledgment of low event count, inability to test PH assumption, and absence of central pathology review
key_concerns: No central pathology review; diagnosis and features (sarcomatoid, necrosis) rely on site abstractors
Low event counts produce wide confidence intervals and preclude competing-risks analysis
Substantial missingness for cT stage (n=38) and cause of death (n=16) handled by exclusion
No external or temporal validation of identified predictors
STROBE checklist not explicitly invoked; limited sensitivity analyses shown
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid, well-reported multicentre observational analysis of a rare RCC subtype with clear clinical implications for surveillance planning; fits a tier-3 urology/oncology journal after minor revisions to clarify missing-data handling and add explicit reporting-standard adherence.
